drafted_from: tool:reframe-video's own row in tools/media-composition/tool-rows.json, tools/media-composition/do-work/reframe-to-a-size.mjs, and the script run on a synthetic 7 second 320x180 clip
start_here: Say to your AI: "Make my 16:9 video vertical for a reel, with the frame following the action." It runs tool:reframe-video and saves the new video in your files.
no_lists_because: It makes a new video in your files from the video you name and keeps no list of its own.
instructions: 1. Find your clip's identity and exact length in bytes in your files (find_file or list_files).

2. Say "Reframe this video to 9:16" with that clip. Optional: aspect_w and aspect_h (default 9 and 16), fill ("crop" fills the frame, "blur" fits the whole picture over a blurred copy, or a colour such as black), follow ("motion" or "brightness"), width and height in pixels.

3. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run and tool tool:reframe-video, passing files as [{name:"source.mp4", identity, bytes}]. The door runs it in a container and answers {"result": {...}}; an error comes back as {"error": "what to change"}.
4. Read result (duration_seconds, width, height, bytes) and files.video, the identity of the reframed video now in your files.

worked_examples.title: A landscape clip made 9:16
worked_examples.ask: Make my video vertical for a reel.
worked_examples.given: read from tools/media-composition/do-work/reframe-to-a-size.mjs and run on a 7 second 320x180 clip: the default crop of 9:16 is the largest that fits without enlarging, 180 tall by 102 wide
